subject: CAIQ evidence entropy & sampling instructions
messages:
From: Tilly Barton <tilly@acmeaudit.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: security_ops@finedgebank.com
Date: 2026-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CAIQ evidence sampling — entropy concerns

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our CAIQ assessment for FinEdge Bank we need to validate a combination of low-entropy operational artefacts (policy docs, owner attestations, config manifests) and high-entropy runtime traces (request logs, KV cache activity, generation traces). A couple of clarifying asks up-front: 

- We need a short note on how Redwood differentiates low- vs high-entropy samples for the purposes of the audit (criteria you apply).
- Example sets: 3 low-entropy artifacts (control descriptions, attestation emails, config exports) and 5 high-entropy traces spanning at least two distinct deployment clusters/regions.
- Any redaction or transformations you apply before handing logs (hashing, token-stripping) must be documented.
- Can you provide a simple sampling matrix and a suggested delivery timeline (3-5 business days ideally)?

Could you also indicate whether the high-entropy traces can be exported as filtered events (we don’t need PII or raw prompts, just telemetry and token-level timing) and list what will be redacted. Attachments are fine as stubs — we only need examples to validate procedures.

Best,
Tilly Barton
Sr. Auditor — Acme Audit

Attachment: audit-scope.pdf (stub)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Tilly Barton <tilly@acmeaudit.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence sampling — entropy concerns

Tilly — thanks for the clear list. Below is the proposed approach and what we can deliver within 3 business days. I’m copying Kim for implementation specifics.

Summary (high level):
- Sampling approach: stratified by CAIQ control family and artifact entropy. Low-entropy = static artifacts (policies, attestations, infra manifests). High-entropy = runtime traces (request/response metadata, KV-cache access patterns, inference trace timing).
- Criteria: artifacts flagged low-entropy if they are human-authored, versioned, and invariant over >7 days. Runtime traces flagged high-entropy if they contain user-influenced inputs or token-level timing (we will strip PII and the actual prompt text).
- Delivery: CAIQ_Sample_Matrix.xlsx (mapping of controls -> example artifacts), control_mapping_snapshot.json (control->owner mapping), plus a set of sanitized runtime traces.

What we will provide (3 business day target):
1) CAIQ_Sample_Matrix.xlsx — spreadsheet mapping each requested control to a representative artifact and confidence score. (attachment)
2) control_mapping_snapshot.json — snapshot of owners and evidence paths for the subset included in the review. (attachment)
3) High-entropy sample set (5 traces) spanning two runtime clusters (us-west1 / us-east4):
   - 2 KV-cache operation extracts (redacted keys, timing only)
   - 3 request-level generation traces (metadata only: request id hashed, tokens redacted, latency per stage)
   - All traces will have identifiers pseudonymized (sha256 hash), no raw prompts or customer identifiers.
4) Documentation: short note on redaction + transformation steps and a screenshot of the evidence staging view in our internal portal.

Delivery notes / ask from you: please confirm the minimum trace window you require (we can capture a 48-hour sliding window or a specific 7-day window if you prefer). Also confirm whether your compliance team needs original timestamps preserved (we will preserve UTC timestamps, do not alter sequence).

Attachments: CAIQ_Sample_Matrix.xlsx; control_mapping_snapshot.json

Thanks — I’ll queue the extraction once Kim confirms retention/redaction knobs.

Jonas Weber
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Cc: Tilly Barton <tilly@acmeaudit.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-15T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence sampling — entropy concerns

Jonas / Tilly — technical details below and samples attached. Forwarding the planned extraction checklist.

Extraction checklist (technical):
- Window: we recommend a 72-hour contiguous window to capture typical traffic variance; we can do 48 / 7 days on request.
- Clusters: us-west1 (primary inference), us-east4 (failover). We will include traces from both.
- Redaction rules:
  * All user-provided prompt text will be stripped; we will keep only request metadata (request_id hashed with sha256, model_id, truncated token count).
  * Any IPs or hostnames will be replaced with 'redacted-host-<n>' placeholders.
  * KV cache keys will be replaced with deterministic hashes; timing and hit/miss counts will be preserved.
  * No customer IDs; we will map internal tenant ids to opaque refs (tenant-01, tenant-02) and include a mapping note.
- Format: newline-delimited JSON events, gzipped. Example stub attached: kv-cache-sample.log (first 20 lines).

Evidence sufficiency note: the audit team typically accepts hashed identifiers + preserved timing as sufficient for control validation (shows correct routing, cache behavior, and TTLs). If FinEdge requires original identifiers for deep lineage, we need a signed data-handling agreement and SAE approval.

Attachments included: kv-cache-sample.log (log stub, 20 lines), runtime-filtered-trace.json (schema example)
